Tipón Archaeological Park

Flowing channels beside agricultural terraces

Current ratingsOpening hoursView the place on the map
Nearby places

Explore

Streams still run through carefully cut channels beside agricultural terraces. The relationship is easier to read by following one supply line rather than looking at every fountain separately: water, retaining walls and cultivation surfaces work as one design.

Planning your visit

60–90 min · Allow this time for the visit itself. Add travel, admission queues and any scheduled tour separately.

What to look for

Flowing channels beside agricultural terraces

From a designated viewing point line up a water outlet with the terrace beneath it. The change of level explains the system better than a photograph of water alone.

History and local experience

Notice how a regular line of terrace walls is interrupted only where water must pass. The arrangement balances usable growing space with a controlled change in water level.

Walking route

  1. Parque Arqueológico de Tipón, Quispicanchi
  2. At the control point ask for the open terrace circuit.
  3. Walk beside one channel to its division or drop, then return along the designated path.
  4. Do not step onto the channel lining for photographs.

Before you go

Visitor questions

How do I reach the site?

At the control point ask for the open terrace circuit. Walk beside one channel to its division or drop, then return along the designated path. Do not step onto the channel lining for photographs.

What should I look for here?

From a designated viewing point line up a water outlet with the terrace beneath it. The change of level explains the system better than a photograph of water alone.

Where can I verify access and admission?

The site authority sets the open sectors and the last admission. Confirm these with the control post, particularly on days with rain or maintenance.
